questions.question: When several queries fire at the same moment in the browser, how do they end up as a single HTTP request?

answer.content:
{"answer":"Simultaneous queries become one HTTP request when the client uses a batching link: `httpBatchLink` (and `httpBatchStreamLink`) collect the queued operations and emit a single request whose path is the comma-joined list of operation paths and whose body carries the array of inputs, combined via `jsonHttpRequester` → `httpRequest`. Plain `httpLink` does not batch — it sends one `universalRequester` call per operation.

- `packages/client/src/links/httpBatchLink.ts` — `httpBatchLink`: builds `batchOps`, does `batchOps.map((op) => op.path).join(',')`, `batchOps.map((op) => op.input)`, and merges all operation abort signals before one `jsonHttpRequester` call.
- `packages/client/src/links/HTTPBatchLinkOptions.ts` — `HTTPBatchLinkOptions` configures batch sizing/behavior; `packages/client/src/links/httpBatchStreamLink.ts` — `httpBatchStreamLink` batches the same way but streams results back.
- `packages/client/src/links/internals/httpUtils.ts` — `jsonHttpRequester` / `httpRequest` is the shared single-fetch transport both use; `packages/client/src/links/httpLink.ts` — `httpLink` / `universalRequester` is the unbatched counterpart.
- Server side, `packages/server/src/unstable-core-do-not-import/http/contentType.ts` — `getRequestInfo` / `jsonContentTypeHandler` parse the batched request (note `maxBatchSize` in `GetRequestInfoOptions`), and `resolveResponse` in `packages/server/src/unstable-core-do-not-import/http/resolveResponse.ts` resolves each call, with `packages/server/src/unstable-core-do-not-import/rpc/envelopes.ts` — `TRPCRequestMessage` giving each batched call its own id.

Missing from the evidence: the actual queue/tick mechanism that decides which concurrent operations land in the same batch (e.g. a dataloader-style scheduler), so I can't say precisely where the grouping happens beyond the `batchOps` aggregation shown.","citations":["component:packages-client-src-links-http-batch-link-ts","code:packages-client-src-links-http-batch-link-ts:http-batch-link","component:packages-client-src-links-http-batch-link-options-ts","code:packages-client-src-links-http-batch-link-options-ts:http-batch-link-options","component:packages-client-src-links-http-batch-stream-link-ts","code:packages-client-src-links-http-batch-stream-link-ts:http-batch-stream-link","component:packages-client-src-links-internals-http-utils-ts","code:packages-client-src-links-internals-http-utils-ts:json-http-requester","code:packages-client-src-links-internals-http-utils-ts:http-request","component:packages-client-src-links-http-link-ts","code:packages-client-src-links-http-link-ts:http-link","code:packages-client-src-links-http-link-ts:universal-requester","component:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-content-type-ts","code:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-content-type-ts:get-request-info","code:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-content-type-ts:get-request-info-options","code:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-content-type-ts:json-content-type-handler","component:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-resolve-response-ts","code:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-resolve-response-ts:resolve-response","component:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-rpc-envelopes-ts","code:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-rpc-envelopes-ts:trpc-request-message"]}

questions.question: If one call in a batched request fails and another succeeds, what HTTP status does the combined response get?

answer.content:
{"answer": "**207 Multi-Status.** `getHTTPStatusCode` collects one status per entry in the batch response array — each error entry maps to its `httpStatus` / error-code-derived status, each success to `200` — and if that set has more than one distinct status, it returns `207`. Only when every entry agrees does the combined response get that single status.

- `packages/server/src/unstable-core-do-not-import/http/getHTTPStatusCode.ts` — `getHTTPStatusCode`, `getHTTPStatusCodeFromError`, `HTTP_CODE_TO_JSONRPC2`. The `httpStatuses.size !== 1 => 207` branch is the exact rule for mixed success/failure batches.
- `packages/server/src/unstable-core-do-not-import/http/resolveResponse.ts` — `resolveResponse`, `initResponse`, `ResolveHTTPRequestOptions` build the (possibly array-shaped) `TRPCResponse` whose statuses get collapsed.
- `packages/server/src/adapters/node-http/nodeHTTPRequestHandler.ts` — `nodeHTTPRequestHandler` writes that response out via `writeResponse`.
- Client side, `packages/client/src/links/httpBatchLink.ts` (`httpBatchLink`) and `packages/client/src/links/httpBatchStreamLink.ts` (`httpBatchStreamLink`) are what issue the batched request that receives that combined status.

Note: the streaming `httpBatchStreamLink` path uses a JSONL response, so the exact status semantics there are not covered by the excerpt evidence.", "citations": ["code:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-get-http-status-code-ts:get-http-status-code", "code:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-get-http-status-code-ts:get-http-status-code-from-error", "code:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-get-http-status-code-ts:http-code-to-jsonrpc2", "component:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-get-http-status-code-ts", "code:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-resolve-response-ts:resolve-response", "code:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-resolve-response-ts:init-response", "component:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-resolve-response-ts", "code:packages-server-src-adapters-node-http-node-http-request-handler-ts:node-http-request-handler", "component:packages-server-src-adapters-node-http-node-http-request-handler-ts", "code:packages-client-src-links-http-batch-link-ts:http-batch-link", "component:packages-client-src-links-http-batch-link-ts", "code:packages-client-src-links-http-batch-stream-link-ts:http-batch-stream-link", "component:packages-client-src-links-http-batch-stream-link-ts"]}

questions.question: How do live subscriptions work over plain HTTP without WebSockets, and how does a client resume after a dropped connection?

answer.content:
{"answer": "Live subscriptions over plain HTTP run as an SSE stream: `httpSubscriptionLink` (`packages/client/src/links/httpSubscriptionLink.ts`) rejects anything but `type === 'subscription'` and feeds the request URL through `sseStreamConsumer` with an `EventSource` (defaulting to `globalThis.EventSource`), deserializing each event via the link transformer.

Resume after a drop works through a tracked `lastEventId`:
- The link keeps `let lastEventId: string | undefined` and injects it into the request input via `inputWithTrackedEventId(input, lastEventId)` every time the URL is (re)built inside `httpSubscriptionLink`, so reconnects resend the last seen event id and the server can continue from there. The stream payload shape carries an optional `id` per event, which is what populates that tracker.
- Connection auth/context travels as query params rather than a first message: `UrlOptionsWithConnectionParams` in `packages/client/src/links/internals/urlWithConnectionParams.ts` documents that for `httpSubscriptionLink`, `connectionParams` are serialized into the `connectionParams` query string (contrast with `wsLink`/`WsConnection`, which sends them via `buildConnectionMessage`). On the server, `parseConnectionParamsFromString`/`parseConnectionParamsFromUnknown` (`packages/server/src/unstable-core-do-not-import/http/parseConnectionParams.ts`) parse them back for `createContext()`.
- The abort path uses `raceAbortSignals(op.signal, ac.signal)`, and connection status is exposed as a `TRPCConnectionState` behavior subject (`packages/client/src/links/internals/subscriptions.ts`), the same state type `WsClient` uses.

One detail is not in the evidence: how the server-side SSE handler interprets the resumed `lastEventId` (the exact replay/resume semantics on the `@trpc/server` HTTP handler side).","citations":["component:packages-client-src-links-http-subscription-link-ts","code:packages-client-src-links-http-subscription-link-ts:http-subscription-link","code:packages-client-src-links-http-subscription-link-ts:http-subscription-link-options","code:packages-client-src-links-http-subscription-link-ts:unstable-http-subscription-link","component:packages-client-src-links-internals-url-with-connection-params-ts","code:packages-client-src-links-internals-url-with-connection-params-ts:url-options-with-connection-params","component:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-parse-connection-params-ts","code:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-parse-connection-params-ts:parse-connection-params-from-string","code:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-parse-connection-params-ts:parse-connection-params-from-unknown","component:packages-client-src-links-internals-subscriptions-ts","code:packages-client-src-links-internals-subscriptions-ts:trpc-connection-state","component:packages-client-src-links-ws-link-ws-client-ws-client-utils-ts","code:packages-client-src-links-ws-link-ws-client-utils-ts:build-connection-message"]}

questions.question: How do I plug the API into an existing Express server?

answer.content:
{"answer": "Mount `createExpressMiddleware` from `packages/server/src/adapters/express.ts` as a normal Express handler — e.g. `app.use('/trpc', createExpressMiddleware({ router: appRouter, createContext }))`. It returns an `express.Handler`, so it drops into an existing server alongside your other routes.

- `createExpressMiddleware` (`packages/server/src/adapters/express.ts`) accepts `NodeHTTPHandlerOptions<TRouter, express.Request, express.Response>`, derives the procedure path from `req.path` (the segment after the last `/`), and delegates to `nodeHTTPRequestHandler`, wrapping failures in the internal exception handler.
- Its options come from `NodeHTTPHandlerOptions` (`packages/server/src/adapters/node-http/types.ts`), which combines the HTTP base handler options with `NodeHTTPCreateContextOption` — so you pass `router` plus an optional `createContext`.
- `CreateExpressContextOptions` (same file) is the `{ req, res }` shape your `createContext` receives; `NodeHTTPRequest`/`NodeHTTPResponse` describe those objects (note `NodeHTTPResponse` allows an optional `flush()` from compression middleware).
- Your router is typed as `AnyRouter` (`packages/server/src/unstable-core-do-not-import/router.ts`), i.e. anything built with `initTRPC`'s router factory (see `appRouter` in `packages/upgrade/test/__fixtures__/hooks/existingRqMix.trpc.tsx` for a minimal example).
- The Fastify path (`fastifyTRPCPlugin` in `packages/server/src/adapters/fastify/fastifyTRPCPlugin.ts`) is the analogous non-Express adapter — useful only as a comparison.

Not in the evidence: a documented code snippet for wiring Express specifically (e.g. `express()` setup/`app.use` call in docs or tests).", "citations": ["component:packages-server-src-adapters-express-ts", "code:packages-server-src-adapters-express-ts:create-express-middleware", "code:packages-server-src-adapters-express-ts:create-express-context-options", "component:packages-server-src-adapters-node-http-types-ts", "code:packages-server-src-adapters-node-http-types-ts:node-http-handler-options", "code:packages-server-src-adapters-node-http-types-ts:node-http-response", "component:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-router-ts", "code:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-router-ts:any-router", "code:packages-upgrade-test-fixtures-hooks-existing-rq-mix-trpc-tsx:app-router", "component:packages-server-src-adapters-fastify-fastify-trpc-plugin-ts", "code:packages-server-src-adapters-fastify-fastify-trpc-plugin-ts:fastify-trpc-plugin"]}

questions.question: What is the server package's unstable-core-do-not-import folder, and why is it named that way?

answer.content:
{"answer":"`packages/server/src/unstable-core-do-not-import/` is the shared core of `@trpc/server`: the primitives every other layer builds on — routers, procedures, builders, middleware, RPC envelopes/codes, error formatting, parsers, transformers, proxies and type utilities. The name is the only signal in the evidence about its status — it marks these internals as unstable and off-limits for direct imports — but no section states the rationale explicitly, so the exact *why* behind the name is not in the evidence.

What's inside:
- `packages/server/src/unstable-core-do-not-import/router.ts` — `Router`, `AnyRouter`, `isRouter`, plus `createRouterFactory`/`callProcedure` (the router core)
- `procedure.ts` (`Procedure`, `AnyProcedure`) and `procedureBuilder.ts` (`ProcedureBuilder`, `createBuilder`, `createProcedureCaller`) — how procedures are defined and executed
- `initTRPC.ts` (`initTRPC`, `TRPCBuilder`) and `rootConfig.ts` (`RootConfig`, `isServerDefault`) — the public entry surface that wraps these internals
- `middleware.ts`, `parser.ts`, `transformer.ts`, `createProxy.ts` — extension points and proxy plumbing
- `rpc/envelopes.ts` (`JSONRPC2`, `TRPCClientIncomingMessage`), `rpc/codes.ts`, `rpc/parseTRPCMessage.ts` — wire protocol
- `error/formatter.ts`, `http/types.ts`, `stream/sse.ts`, `clientish/inference.ts`, `types.ts`, `utils.ts` — shared types, error shapes and helpers

questions.question: Is there an automated tool to move my React code from the old hooks-style integration to the new TanStack Query style?

answer.content:
{"answer":"Yes — the `@trpc/upgrade` package (`container:packages-upgrade`) ships exactly that: a codemod transform in `packages/upgrade/src/transforms/hooksToOptions.ts` (`component:packages-upgrade-src-transforms-hooks-to-options-ts`) that rewrites hooks-style calls into TanStack Query style.

- `hookToOptions` (`code:packages-upgrade-src-transforms-hooks-to-options-ts:hook-to-options`) maps each legacy hook to its new form: `useQuery`/`useSuspenseQuery` → `queryOptions` from `@tanstack/react-query`, `useInfiniteQuery` → `infiniteQueryOptions`, etc.
- `utilMap` (`code:packages-upgrade-src-transforms-hooks-to-options-ts:util-map`) does the same for utils calls: `fetch` → `fetchQuery`/`queryOptions`, `prefetch` → `prefetchQuery`/`queryOptions`, `fetchInfinite` → `fetchInfiniteQuery`/`infiniteQueryOptions`, and so on.
- `transform` (`code:packages-upgrade-src-transforms-hooks-to-options-ts:transform`, lines 63–443) is the main jscodeshift-style entry that walks the AST and applies those mappings.
- Test fixtures under `packages/upgrade/test/__fixtures__/hooks/` exercise it against real hook code — e.g. `optimistic-update.trpc.tsx` (`component:packages-upgrade-test-fixtures-hooks-optimistic-update-trpc-tsx`) and `utilities.trpc.tsx` (`component:packages-upgrade-test-fixtures-hooks-utilities-trpc-tsx`), which cover optimistic updates and utils (`fetch`/`prefetch`/paginated queries).

questions.question: Once an adapter hands over an incoming HTTP request, where is it decoded, run against the right procedure, and turned back into a response?

answer.content:
{"answer":"The pipeline lives in `nodeHTTPRequestHandler` (`packages/server/src/adapters/node-http/nodeHTTPRequestHandler.ts`): it converts the adapter's Node req/res into a WHATWG `Request`, hands that to `resolveResponse`, then writes the resulting `Response` back out.

- **Decode**: `incomingMessageToRequest` (`packages/server/src/adapters/node-http/incomingMessageToRequest.ts`) builds the `Request` via `createHeaders` and `createBody` (streamed body, max-size limit, abort wiring).
- **Dispatch/run**: `resolveResponse` (`packages/server/src/unstable-core-do-not-import/http/resolveResponse.ts`) takes the decoded request plus `createContext`/`onError` and returns a `Response`; the procedure call shape it consumes is described by `TRPCRequestInfoProcedureCall` / `TRPCRequestInfo` (`packages/server/src/unstable-core-do-not-import/http/types.ts`).
- **Encode**: `writeResponse` (`packages/server/src/adapters/node-http/writeResponse.ts`) copies status/headers and streams the body via `writeResponseBody` / `writeResponseBodyChunk` onto the raw `NodeHTTPResponse` (`packages/server/src/adapters/node-http/types.ts`).

Same three steps for other adapters: `fastifyRequestHandler` (`packages/server/src/adapters/fastify/fastifyRequestHandler.ts`) reuses `incomingMessageToRequest` + `resolveResponse` and sends via `res.send`; `fetchRequestHandler` (`packages/server/src/adapters/fetch/fetchRequestHandler.ts`) skips the Node conversion since it already has a `Request`. `internal_exceptionHandler` in the node handler covers failures before a response is written.

The selected scope (`@trpc/openapi` test helpers) is unrelated to this pipeline.","citations":["code:packages-server-src-adapters-node-http-node-http-request-handler-ts:node-http-request-handler","code:packages-server-src-adapters-node-http-incoming-message-to-request-ts:incoming-message-to-request","code:packages-server-src-adapters-node-http-incoming-message-to-request-ts:create-headers","code:packages-server-src-adapters-node-http-incoming-message-to-request-ts:create-body","code:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-resolve-response-ts:resolve-response","code:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-types-ts:trpc-request-info-procedure-call","code:packages-server-src-unstable-core-do-not-import-http-types-ts:trpc-request-info","code:packages-server-src-adapters-node-http-write-response-ts:write-response","code:packages-server-src-adapters-node-http-write-response-ts:write-response-body","code:packages-server-src-adapters-node-http-types-ts:node-http-response","code:packages-server-src-adapters-fastify-fastify-request-handler-ts:fastify-request-handler","code:packages-server-src-adapters-fetch-fetch-request-handler-ts:fetch-request-handler","code:packages-server-src-adapters-node-http-node-http-request-handler-ts:internal-exception-handler"]}
